basic_info.name: MERT (Acoustic Music Understanding Model). Variants: music2vec-v1, MERT-v0, MERT-v0-public (95M), MERT-v1-95M, MERT-v1-330M.
basic_info.org: M-A-P consortium (m-a-p.ai) + University of Manchester, University of Sheffield, Carnegie Mellon, HKUST, QMUL, BAAI, et al. Lead authors: Yizhi Li, Ruibin Yuan, Ge Zhang. Published at ICLR 2024.

architecture.backbone: HuBERT-style Transformer (speech-SSL stack: 1D conv front end + 12-layer 768-d Transformer at 95M, 24-layer 1024-d at 330M) trained on raw audio at 75 Hz frame rate.
architecture.input_modality: audio only (24 kHz mono). No text tower — MERT itself is not a joint-embedding model.
architecture.training_objective: Masked language modeling (HuBERT-style masked prediction) with two teacher tokenizers: EnCodec RVQ-VAE (8 codebooks, acoustic teacher) and Constant-Q Transform quantization (musical teacher for pitch/harmony inductive bias); in-batch noise mixup augmentation, Pre-LN for stability.
architecture.embedding_output: Frame-level hidden states: 768-d at 75 Hz (95M, 12 layers) or 1024-d (330M, 24 layers); no built-in global embedding — downstream code typically layer-averages or time-pools (CLaMP 3 averages across all layers and time steps per 5 s clip). No joint text embedding dim.

data.training_data: MERT-v1-330M: ~160K h music audio (mix of open and in-house sources, exact composition not fully disclosed); MERT-v1-95M: ~20K h; MERT-v0-public: 900 h open (Music4all). Teacher tokens from EnCodec + CQT. No music-text pairs (contrastive not used).

performance.benchmarks: SSL-family (MARBLE linear-probe suite, 14-task original eval): MERT-v1-330M MARBLE avg 74.4 — superseded by MuQ (77.0) and behind MusicFM (75.4) on the 9-task MARBLE comparison. Strong MTT tagging ROC-AUC 91.3 but weak key detection (65.6 refined) and Nsynth instrument 72.6. SOTA overall at 2023 release; still relevant as the frozen audio feature extractor inside CLaMP 3 (audio-text retrieval SOTA at CLaMP 3 release, ACL 2025 Findings).
performance.vs_clap: No direct music-text benchmark of its own (no text tower). As MuLan-style contrastive backbone (MERT-MuLan, 130K h pairs, paper-reported): MTT zero-shot tagging ROC-AUC 75.5 / PR-AUC 24.6 vs LAION-CLAP 73.9 / 25.0 — roughly at CLAP level, below MuQ-MuLan 79.3. As feature extractor feeding CLaMP 3, exceeds CLAP on multilingual audio retrieval.

availability.license: Model weights CC-BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial); code Apache-2.0. Production use requires separate agreement. Requires torch + trust_remote_code custom code, not pure numpy.

fit_for_local_playlist.sample_rate: 24 kHz for MERT-v1 (75 Hz feature rate); earlier MERT-v0/music2vec were 16 kHz @ 50 Hz. Repo standard 48 kHz needs resampling.
fit_for_local_playlist.inference_cost: 95M (v1-95M) or 330M (v1-330M) params; ~1.3 GB fp32 for 95M. CPU inference is slow (authors note Jukebox-scale inefficiency only for 7B models, but 330M EnCodec-tokenizer training was GPU-heavy; inference itself is a standard transformer) [uncertain for exact per-track latency].
fit_for_local_playlist.full_track_context: 5 s training context (relative position embeddings allow longer); long tracks handled only by windowing — CLaMP 3 windows 5 s clips up to 640 s and average-pools.
fit_for_local_playlist.frame_level_support: Yes — native 75 Hz frame-level hidden states, well-suited to section-level/FIGMA-style logic when layer-selected.
fit_for_local_playlist.multilingual_queries: None by itself. Via CLaMP 3 wrapper: 100 languages (XLM-R text tower, 27 trained).
fit_for_local_playlist.retrieval_steering: None — plain SSL feature extractor; no text alignment, no attribute control.

uncertain: Exact composition and licensing of the 160K h MERT-v1 pre-training mix (partially disclosed)
CPU per-track inference latency for MERT-v1-330M
